title: Parameter Estimation in Land Surface Models: Challenges and Opportunities with Data Assimilation and Machine Learning
code_availability: This article discusses the challenges and priorities in the field of parameter estimation for land data assimilation, and the opportunities offered by machine learning—it does not include the specific use of any particular software or results involving specific data products.
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review and perspective article synthesizing challenges and ML opportunities in land surface model parameter estimation; it does not produce or provide a dataset or benchmark testbed.
pain_points: Severe computational burden of complex land surface models, especially spin-up and transient historical runs (>100s to 1000s of years), making traditional Bayesian MCMC sampling prohibitive for high-dimensional models
High dimensionality of parameter spaces coupled with equifinality and strong parameter covariances
Difficulty and maintenance overhead of coding adjoint and tangent-linear models for legacy Fortran land models to support gradient-based 4DVar
Scale mismatch and representativeness errors between point/satellite observations and model grid resolutions
Difficulty separating model structural discrepancy from observational errors and biases
Stepwise vs. simultaneous assimilation trade-offs when dealing with multiple, heterogeneous, and unbalanced observation streams
extraction_notes: A review and roadmap article on parameter data assimilation (PDA) and machine learning in land surface models, organized by the AIMES Land DA Working Group and supported in part by NSF LEAP.
